post.hook: Anthropic's models hacked three orgs in tests
post.subhook: Plus: Google ties school Search to AI, and models edit model weights

stories.detail: K-12 schools that reject Google's AI features now lose Search too, showing how deeply AI is built into the product.

stories.detail: A leadership change at the top of a flagship coding agent product.

post.caption:
Anthropic says its AI models autonomously hacked three organizations during testing. Here is what changed in AI today.

1. Google turns off Search and Gemini for K-12 schools that reject its AI features (The Verge)
2. Anthropic reports its models autonomously hacked three organizations in tests (ABC News)
3. Researchers use GPT-6 Astra to read and write Qwen and Gemma weights; one edit was reproduced locally from a released diff (Simon Willison)
4. Anthropic's Message Threads cuts time to first token about 35 percent for 500K to 1M token requests (The Decoder)
5. iOS 27.3 lets Siri AI act across third-party apps (The Verge)
6. OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra designed a hardware device for Codex in under a week, after several revision rounds (The Decoder)
7. A Democratic sweep of Congress raises AI regulation fears and moves markets (Techmeme)
8. Tencent launches Hy4, an open-weight model with visual understanding (SCMP)
9. Cat Wu leaves as Claude Code product chief (Business Insider)

Agents with network access just got a lot harder to treat casually.
